steps.title: Filtration
steps.say: Blood arrives in the afferent arteriole and leaves through the efferent. In the lens, plasma is pushed through three layers: the fenestrated endothelium, the negatively charged basement membrane and the slits between podocyte feet. Water and small solutes cross, but albumin and red cells are held back. Glomerular pressure of 55 millimetres of mercury, minus 15 in Bowman's capsule and 30 of plasma oncotic pressure, leaves a net 10. That makes 125 millilitres a minute, about 180 litres a day.

steps.title: Proximal tubule
steps.say: Inside a proximal tubule cell, the sodium potassium pump on the blood side keeps cell sodium low, so sodium flows in from the lumen on SGLT2 with glucose and on the sodium hydrogen exchanger. Water follows straight through aquaporins and between the cells. So the parcel loses about 65 percent of its volume, yet its osmolality stays at 300. All of the glucose and about 80 percent of the bicarbonate are taken back here.

steps.title: Descending limb
steps.say: Unfold the loop of Henle into a hairpin. The thin descending limb lets water through but not salt. As it dives into an ever saltier medulla, water leaves by osmosis, so the fluid keeps pace with the interstitium around it. By the tip of the loop it is about 1200 milliosmoles per kilogram, and only about 9 percent of the filtrate is left.

steps.title: Thick ascending limb
steps.say: Now the wall flips. Inside a thick ascending limb cell, the N K 2 C L cotransporter takes up sodium, potassium and two chlorides, and potassium leaks back out through ROMK, which makes the lumen positive and drives magnesium and calcium between the cells. There are no water channels, so salt leaves without water and the fluid dilutes to about 100. That pumped salt builds the 300 to 1200 gradient, and it is exactly what furosemide blocks.

steps.title: Macula densa, DCT
steps.say: The limb returns to touch its own glomerulus at the macula densa, which senses the salt arriving. In the distal convoluted tubule, the thiazide-sensitive sodium chloride carrier removes a little more salt, and the wall is still water-tight, so the fluid stays dilute, at about 90.

steps.title: Aldosterone, ADH
steps.say: In the collecting duct, look inside a principal cell. Aldosterone makes it take up sodium through ENaC and secrete potassium through ROMK. ADH binds the V2 receptor on the blood side, cyclic A M P moves vesicles of aquaporin-2 into the apical membrane, and water leaves toward the 300 milliosmole cortex. The fluid climbs from about 90 back to nearly 300.

steps.title: Concentrated urine
steps.say: The duct then runs down through the same gradient the loop built, and water keeps leaving into the hypertonic medulla. The ledger shows where all the filtrate went: about two thirds in the proximal tubule, much of the rest in the descending limb and the collecting duct. The urine ends at over 1100 milliosmoles per kilogram, with well under 1 percent of the filtrate left. That is about 1 litre a day from 180.
